paragraphs: In this section, unless otherwise specified, references to "we," "our," "us" and "our company" refer to Gyre Therapeutics, Inc. and our majority indirectly owned subsidiary, Beijing Continent Pharmaceuticals Co., Ltd. (d/b/a Gyre Pharmaceuticals Co., Ltd.) ("Gyre Pharmaceuticals").

We are a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the development and commercialization of small-molecule therapies for the treatment of organ fibrosis and inflammatory diseases. We operate through our majority indirectly owned subsidiary, Gyre Pharmaceuticals, in the PRC, and through our U.S. operations headquartered in San Diego, California.

In the PRC, we have established a strong commercial and operational foundation in fibrotic diseases through the successful development and commercialization of ETUARY® (pirfenidone), which has generated consistent revenue and positioned us as a leading participant in the treatment of pulmonary fibrosis.

Fibrotic diseases affect large patient populations worldwide and involve complex, multi-stage biological processes driven by multiple molecular pathways. Given this complexity, therapies that modulate key profibrotic signaling pathways may offer meaningful clinical benefit; however, effective treatment may require targeting mechanisms across different stages of disease progression.

Building on our commercialization experience and infrastructure in the PRC, we have expanded our presence into the United States to advance the clinical development of our innovative pipeline, including F351 (Hydronidone), our lead product candidate for liver fibrosis.

Our strategy is to leverage our established commercial portfolio to support and de-risk the advancement of late-stage product candidates, expand approved products into additional indications, and build a diversified pipeline targeting significant unmet medical needs in fibrosis and related inflammatory diseases.

On March 2, 2026, we entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger and Reorganization (the "Merger Agreement") with Cullgen Inc., a Delaware corporation ("Cullgen"), and Helix Merger Sub Corp., a Delaware corporation and wholly owned subsidiary of Gyre ("Merger Sub"), pursuant to which, among other matters, and subject to the satisfaction or waiver of the conditions set forth in the Merger Agreement, Merger Sub will merge with and into Cullgen, with Cullgen continuing as a wholly owned subsidiary of Gyre and the surviving corporation of the merger (the "Merger"). The Merger is intended to qualify for federal income tax purposes as a tax-free reorganization under the provisions of Section 368(a) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended.

The consummation of the Merger is subject to certain closing conditions, including, among other things, (1) approval by the requisite Cullgen stockholders of the adoption and approval of the Merger Agreement and the transactions contemplated thereby, and (2) a filing under the HSR Act.
There can be no assurances that the Merger will be successfully consummated, and the intended benefits of the Merger may not be realized.

Our commercial portfolio establishes our presence as a revenue-generating biopharmaceutical company and serves as the operational and financial platform for our long-term growth strategy. In the PRC, we have built a focused commercial franchise centered on fibrosis and related diseases, anchored by ETUARY® (pirfenidone) and expanded by Etorel® (nintedanib), the two standard-of-care antifibrotic therapies approved for the treatment of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis ("IPF"). We have further broadened our commercial reach with Contiva® (avatrombopag), extending into hematologic conditions associated with chronic liver disease. These products provide recurring revenue, strengthen our market relationships, and support our investment in an innovative pipeline.
We are focused on commercializing therapies for the treatment of pulmonary fibrosis and working to solidify our position as a leader in this space.

Pirfenidone is a small-molecule anti-fibrotic therapy for the treatment of IPF. It was first approved in Japan and subsequently approved in the PRC, the European Union ("EU"), and the United States. These approvals were obtained by different sponsors in their respective jurisdictions under separate regulatory frameworks.

Pulmonary fibrosis is caused by activation of alveolar cells after epithelial damage, which secretes a series of pro-inflammatory cytokines, activating fibroblast proliferation and myofibroblast differentiation and reducing the rate of apoptosis. ETUARY® reduces Type I Collagen expression by inhibiting the expression of pro-fibrogenic mediators, including TGF-ß1, platelet-derived growth factor ("PDGF") and fibroblast growth factor, which ultimately reduces fibroblast proliferation and collagen fiber synthesis and decreases extracellular matrix accumulation. It also inhibits TNF-α, IL-1 and other inflammatory mediators, thus reducing the inflammatory response.

headings: Summary of Risk Factors
Risks Related to the Merger with Cullgen
There is no assurance when or if the Merger will be completed. Any delay in completing the Merger may substantially reduce the potential benefits that we expect to obtain from the Merger.
The issuance, or expected issuance, of our common stock in connection with the Merger could decrease the market price of our common stock.
The intended benefits of the Merger may not be realized.
Our directors and officers may have interests in the Merger that are different from, or in addition to, those of our stockholders generally that may influence them to support or approve the Merger.
The announcement and pendency of the Merger could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations or business prospects.

Certain provisions of the Merger Agreement may discourage third parties from submitting competing proposals, including proposals that may be superior to the arrangements contemplated by the Merger Agreement.

The Exchange Ratio is not adjustable based on the market price of our common stock, so the Merger consideration at the Closing may have a greater or lesser value than at the time the Merger Agreement was signed.
We are expected to incur substantial expenses related to the Merger with Cullgen.
Failure to complete the Merger could negatively affect the value of our common stock and our future business and financial results.
The Merger may be completed even though material adverse changes may result from the announcement of the Merger, industry-wide changes or other causes.
We are substantially dependent on our remaining employees, key contractors and consultants to facilitate the consummation of the Merger.
Risks Related to Our Financial Condition and Capital Requirements
Raising additional funds by issuing securities or through licensing arrangements may cause dilution to stockholders, restrict our operations or require us to relinquish proprietary rights.
Our high gross margin during the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 may not be sustainable.
Our five largest customers accounted for a substantial amount of our revenue during the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, which subjects us to concentration risks.
We may face risk regarding the obsolescence of our inventories.
If our intangible assets are impaired, our results of operations and financial condition may be adversely affected.
We may be subject to credit risk in collecting trade receivables due from our customers.
We have historically received government grants and have been entitled to preferential tax treatment, but we may not continue to receive government financial incentives in the future.
Risks Related to Our Business Operations and Product Candidates
Liver fibrosis is an area of our focus, and our key product candidate in this area is Hydronidone. Our future clinical trials for Hydronidone may not be successful.

You should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below and all information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K before deciding to invest in our common stock. If any of the following risks actually occur, our business, financial condition, results of operations and growth prospects may be materially and adversely affected. In that event, the trading price of our common stock could decline, and you could lose all or part of your investment. Moreover, some of the factors, events and contingencies discussed below may have occurred in the past, but the disclosures below are not representations as to whether or not the factors, events or contingencies have occurred in the past and instead reflect our beliefs and opinions as to the factors, events, or contingencies that could materially and adversely affect us in the future.
Investing in our securities involves a high degree of risk. Below please find a summary of the principal risks we face. These risks are discussed more fully below.
• There is no assurance when or if the Merger will be completed. Any delay in completing the Merger may substantially reduce the potential benefits that we expect to obtain from the Merger.

• Our business is significantly dependent on the sales of ETUARY®, one of our marketed products in the PRC, amid a competitive landscape, and there is a possibility that we may not be able to sustain or boost the sales volume, pricing, and profitability of ETUARY®.

• There is a risk that our marketed products in the PRC, ETUARY®, Etorel® and Contiva®, along with any other products that we may receive approval for and commercialize in the future, may not attain sufficient market acceptance among physicians, healthcare facilities, pharmacies, patients, third-party payers, and the broader medical community, which is crucial for their commercial viability.

• The future of our business and financial outcomes is largely contingent on the progress and success of our product candidates in clinical and preclinical stages, such as ETUARY® for future indications in the PRC, F573 in the PRC, and Hydronidone in the PRC and in additional markets beyond the PRC. We face the risk of not being able to finalize their clinical development, secure necessary regulatory approvals, or accomplish their market launch successfully, or we may encounter substantial setbacks in these processes.

Pirfenidone is a small-molecule anti-fibrotic therapy for the treatment of IPF. It was first approved in Japan and subsequently approved in the PRC, the EU, and the United States. These approvals were obtained by different sponsors in their respective jurisdictions under separate regulatory frameworks.

In the PRC, we conducted independent research and development to support our regulatory submission and received first-in-class approval in 2011 as a National Category 1.1 New Drug. We commercialized pirfenidone under the brand name ETUARY®, which was included in the NRDL in 2017 and has since maintained a leading market position.

In addition to IPF, we are pursuing potential label expansion into additional indications in the PRC, including PD, for which, in 2025, we completed enrollment of 272 patients in our 52-week Phase 3 trial, and RILI, including cases with or without immune-related pneumonitis, for which the NMPA approved our clinical trial application in March 2025, and we expect to initiate an adaptive Phase 2/3 study in the first half of 2026.
Etorel® (nintedanib esilate soft capsules)

In May 2024, Gyre Pharmaceuticals entered into a comprehensive agreement with Jiangsu Wangao Pharmaceuticals Co., Ltd. to obtain the drug registration certificate for Etorel® (nintedanib) and become the marketing authorization holder in the PRC. Etorel® is approved as a standard-of-care therapy for IPF, SSc-ILD, and PF-ILD. The addition of Etorel® to our commercial portfolio expanded treatment options for patients and strengthened Gyre's leading position in the pulmonary fibrosis market. Commercialization of Etorel® in the PRC commenced in June 2025.

On November 7, 2025, the NHSA released the Announcement of the Winning Bids for the National Centralized Drug Procurement, under which Etorel® was selected. As of the filing date, we are in the process of entering into procurement contracts with various participating hospitals under the National Centralized Drug Procurement program. We are currently assessing the potential impact of this development on its future operating performance.

In June 2021, Gyre Pharmaceuticals acquired avatrombopag maleate tablets pursuant to a transfer agreement with Nanjing Healthnice Pharmaceutical Technology Co., Ltd. Avatrombopag is an oral thrombopoietin receptor agonist. In June 2024, the NMPA approved avatrombopag maleate tablets for the treatment of TP associated with CLD in adult patients undergoing elective diagnostic procedures or therapy. In January 2025, the NMPA approved an additional indication for chronic ITP. Gyre Pharmaceuticals commenced commercialization of avatrombopag under the brand name Contiva® in the PRC in March 2025.

Hydronidone is our lead development candidate for the treatment of liver fibrosis. It is a structurally modified derivative of pirfenidone designed to optimize metabolic properties while targeting the TGF-β1 signaling pathway, a key mediator of fibrogenesis. We are developing Hydronidone for two primary indications: CHB-associated liver fibrosis in the PRC and MASH-associated liver fibrosis in the United States. Hydronidone represents our primary liver-focused development program and reflects our commitment to advancing therapies targeting both viral- and metabolic-associated liver fibrosis.

paragraphs: 本節中，除非另有說明，提及「我們」、「我們的」、「我們」及「本公司」均指 Gyre Therapeutics, Inc. 以及我們間接控股的 majority 子公司 Beijing Continent Pharmaceuticals Co., Ltd. (d/b/a Gyre Pharmaceuticals Co., Ltd.) ("Gyre Pharmaceuticals")。
我們是一家商業階段的生物製藥公司，專注於開發及商業化小分子療法，用以治療器官纖維化及發炎性疾病。我們透過我們間接控股的 majority 子公司 Gyre Pharmaceuticals 在中國大陸運作，並透過我們位於美國加州聖地牙哥的美國運營中心。
在中國大陸，我們已建立在纖維化疾病領域的強大商業與運營基礎，透過 ETUARY® (pirfenidone) 的成功開發與商業化，該產品已產生穩定收入，並使我們成為治療肺纖維化的領先參與者。
纖維化疾病在全球影響大量患者羣體，並涉及複雜、多階段的生物學過程，由多種分子路徑驅動。考慮到這種複雜性，調節關鍵促纖維化訊號傳導路徑的療法可能提供重要的臨牀效益；然而，有效的治療可能需要針對不同疾病進展階段的機制。
基於我們在中國大陸的商業化經驗與基礎設施，我們已擴展至美國，以推進我們創新產品線的臨牀開發，包括 F351 (Hydronidone)，這是我們針對肝纖維化的領先產品候選藥物。
我們的策略是利用我們已建立的商業產品組合，以支持並降低晚期產品候選藥物的推進風險，擴展已核准產品至更多適應症，並建立一個針對纖維化及相關發炎性疾病重大未滿足醫療需求的多元化產品線。

2026 年 3 月 2 日，我們與 Cullgen Inc.，一家特拉華州公司 ("Cullgen")，以及 Helix Merger Sub Corp.，一家特拉華州公司且為 Gyre 的 wholly owned 子公司 ("Merger Sub") 籤訂了合併與重組協議 ("Merger Agreement")，根據此協議，除其他事項外，並在滿足或豁免 Merger Agreement 所列條件後，Merger Sub 將與 Cullgen 合併，Cullgen 繼續作為 Gyre 的 wholly owned 子公司，並為合併後的存續公司 ("Merger")。此合併旨在符合美國聯邦所得稅目的，作為根據 1986 年內政部所得稅法第 368(a) 條項規定的稅務無負擔重組。
合併的完成需符合若干關閉條件，包括但不限於：(1) Cullgen 股東對採納及批准 Merger Agreement 及其所預期交易的批准，以及 (2) 根據 HSR 法案進行的申報。
本公司無法保證此合併將能順利完成，且此合併預期的效益可能無法實現。

我們的商業產品組合確立了本公司作為具營收能力的生物製藥公司的地位，並作為本公司長期成長策略的運營與財務平台。在中國大陸，我們已建立一個專注於纖維化及其相關疾病的商業品牌，以ETUARY®（pirfenidone）為核心，並透過Etorel®（nintedanib）擴展，這兩種為治療特發性肺纖維化（"IPF"）所批准的標準療法。我們進一步拓展了商業版圖，透過Contiva®（avatrombopag）進入與慢性肝病相關的血液學疾病。這些產品提供持續性營收，強化我們的市場關係，並支持我們在創新產品線上的投資。
本公司專注於商業化用以治療肺纖維化的療法，並努力鞏固本公司在該領域的領導地位。
Pirfenidone是一種小分子抗纖維化療法，用以治療IPF。它首先在日本獲准，隨後在中國大陸、歐盟（"EU"）及美國獲准。這些核准是由不同申辦人根據各自管轄區域的獨立監管架構所取得。

肺纖維化是由於上皮損傷後肺泡細胞活化所引起，會分泌一系列促發炎性細胞激素，活化纖維母細胞增殖與肌成纖維細胞分化，並降低細胞凋亡率。ETUARY®透過抑制促纖維化媒介物質的表現，包括TGF-ß1、血小板衍生成長因子（"PDGF"）及纖維母細胞成長因子，來降低I型膠原蛋白的表現，最終減少纖維母細胞增殖與膠原纖維合成，並降低細胞外基質的累積。它同時也會抑制TNF-α、IL-1及其他發炎媒介物質，從而降低發炎反應。

paragraphs: 您應閱讀以下對我們財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析，並與本年度10-K表報表中所附之經審計財務報表及相關附註一併參考。本討論及其他部分包含前瞻性陳述，涉及風險與不確定性，例如我們的計畫、目標、預期及意圖之陳述。我們實際結果可能與這些前瞻性陳述所討論之內容有重大差異。導致此等差異之因素包括，但不僅限於，本報告中「風險因素」部分所討論之因素。您應仔細閱讀本年度10-K表報表中「對前瞻性陳述之警示」及「風險因素」部分，以瞭解可能導致實際結果與下文所述結果有重大差異之重要因素。
本公司為一家商業階段之生物製藥公司，專注於開發及商業化用於治療器官纖維化及發炎性疾病之小分子療法。我們透過我們間接控股之子公司Gyre Pharmaceuticals在中國大陸運作，並透過美國總部設於加州聖地牙哥之美國運營部門運作。
我們的策略是利用我們已建立之商業產品組合，以支持並降低晚期產品候選藥物之推進風險，擴展已核准產品至更多適應症，並建立一個針對纖維化及相關發炎性疾病重大未滿足醫療需求之多元化產品管道。

於 2026 年 3 月 2 日，本公司與 Cullgen 及 Merger Sub 簽訂合併協議，根據該協議，除其他事項外，並依合併協議中所列條件之達成或豁免，Merger Sub 將與 Cullgen 合併，Cullgen 繼續作為本公司之 wholly owned subsidiary，並為合併後之存續公司。此合併旨在符合聯邦所得稅目的，依 1986 年內政部稅收法典第 368(a) 節之規定，作為免稅重組。
合併之完成需符合若干關閉條件，包括，但不僅限於，(1) Cullgen股東對採納及批准合併協議及該協議所預期之交易之必要批准，以及(2) 根據HSR法案之 filings。
無法保證此合併將成功完成，且合併預期之好處可能無法實現。
Pirfenidone為一種小分子抗纖維化療法，用於治療IPF。其於日本首先獲批准，隨後在中國大陸、歐盟及美國獲批准。這些批准由不同之申辦人根據其各自之管轄區域及不同之監管架構取得。
於中國大陸，我們進行獨立研究與開發以支持我們的監管申請，並於2011年獲得第一類新藥（National Category 1.1 New Drug）的核准。我們以ETUARY®為品牌名稱商業化吡非尼酮，該藥品於2017年納入國家基本藥物目錄（NRDL），並持續保持領先的市場地位。
除 IPF 之外，我們正在尋求在中國大陸拓展標籤至其他適應症，包括 PD，於 2025 年，我們在 52 週第三期試驗中完成 272 名病患的入組，以及 RILI，包括有或無免疫相關肺炎的案例，於 2025 年 3 月，國家藥品監督管理局批准我們的臨牀試驗申請，我們預期於 2026 年第一季啟動適應性第二期/第三期試驗。
Etorel® (nintedanib esilate soft capsules)

2024 年 5 月，Gyre Pharmaceuticals 與江蘇萬高製藥股份有限公司簽訂全面協議，取得 Etorel® (nintedanib) 的藥品註冊證書，並成為中國大陸的上市許可持有人。Etorel® 被批准作為 IPF、SSc-ILD 及 PF-ILD 的標準治療方案。將 Etorel® 加入我們的商業產品組合，擴展了病患的治療選擇，並強化了 Gyre 在肺纖維化市場的領導地位。Etorel® 在中國大陸的商業化於 2025 年 6 月開始。
2025 年 11 月 7 日，國家醫療保障局發布國家集中藥品採購中標結果公告，Etorel® 被選中。截至申報日，我們正在與參與國家集中藥品採購計劃的各醫院簽訂採購合約。我們目前正在評估此發展對未來營運表現的潛在影響。

2021 年 6 月，Gyre Pharmaceuticals 根據與南京健康 nice 製藥科技有限公司的轉讓協議，取得 avatrombopag maleate 薄片。Avatrombopag 是一種口服的血小板生成素受體激動劑。2024 年 6 月，國家藥品監督管理局批准 avatrombopag maleate 薄片用於治療成人患者在選擇性診斷程序或治療中與 CLD 相關的 TP。2025 年 1 月，國家藥品監督管理局批准另一個適應症為慢性 ITP。Gyre Pharmaceuticals 於 2025 年 3 月在中國大陸以 Contiva® 商標開始商業化 avatrombopag。

Hydronidone 是我們用來治療肝纖維化的領先開發候選藥物。它是 pirfenidone 的結構改良衍生物，設計用以優化代謝特性，同時針對 TGF-β1 信號傳導路徑，這是纖維化的重要媒介。我們正在開發 Hydronidone 用於兩個主要適應症：中國大陸的 CHB 相關肝纖維化，以及美國的 MASH 相關肝纖維化。Hydronidone 代表我們主要的肝臟專注開發計畫，並反映我們致力於進展針對病毒性和代謝相關肝纖維化的治療方案。

headings: 風險因素總覽
與與 Cullgen 合併相關的風險
無法保證合併何時或是否會完成。任何延誤完成合併的情況，可能會大幅降低我們預期從合併中獲得的潛在好處。
我們普通股的發行，或預期發行，與合併有關，可能會降低我們普通股的市場價格。
合併預期的效益可能無法實現。
我們的董事及高階管理人員可能在合併中有與我們股東一般利益不同，或額外的利益，這可能會影響他們支持或批准合併的決定。
合併的公告及進行中，可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果或業務前景產生不利影響。
合併協議的某些條款可能會阻止第三方提出競爭性提案，包括可能優於合併協議所預期安排的提案。
交換比率無法根據本公司普通股的市價進行調整，因此在交割時的合併對價可能高於或低於簽訂合併協議時的價值。
我們預期會因與 Cullgen 的合併產生顯著的費用。
未能完成合併可能會對本公司普通股的價值以及未來的業務與財務結果產生負面影響。
即使因合併公告、產業範圍內的變化或其他原因導致重大不利變動，合併仍可能完成。
我們極度依賴現有員工、關鍵承包商及顧問以促進合併的完成。
與我們財務狀況及資金需求相關的風險
透過發行證券或授權安排籌措額外資金可能會導致股東權益稀釋、限制我們的業務運作或要求我們放棄專屬權利。
我們在 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日結止的年度中高毛利率，可能無法持續
本公司五大客戶在2025年及2024年財務年度中，佔據了我們營業收入的相當大比例，使我們面臨集中風險。
我們可能面臨我們存貨過時的風險。
若我們的無形資產發生減值，將可能對我們的營運成果與財務狀況產生不利影響。
我們可能面臨因應客戶應收帳款而產生的信用風險。
我們歷來曾獲得政府補助，並享有優惠稅務待遇，但未來可能無法持續獲得政府財務補助。
與本公司營運及產品候選藥物相關的風險
肝纖維化為我們的重點研究領域，我們在該領域的關鍵產品候選藥物為Hydronidone。我們未來針對Hydronidone的臨牀試驗可能無法成功。
paragraphs: 下列段落包含可能對我們業務與營運產生重大不利影響的最主要因素。您在決定投資本公司普通股之前，應謹慎考量下列所述的風險與不確定性，以及本年度報告表10-K所包含的所有資訊。若有任何上述風險實際發生，可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果與成長前景造成重大且不利的影響。在此情況下，本公司普通股的交易價格可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。此外，部分在下列討論中提及的因素、事件與潛在狀況可能已發生於過去，但下列披露內容並不代表這些因素、事件或潛在狀況是否已發生於過去，而是反映我們對未來可能對我們造成重大且不利影響的因素、事件或潛在狀況的觀點與看法。
投資本公司證券涉及高度風險。請參閱下列我們所面臨的主要風險總結。這些風險在下文中會有更詳細的說明。
• 無法保證合併（Merger）何時或是否會完成。若完成合併的過程有所延宕，可能大幅降低我們預期從合併中獲得的潛在好處。
• 我們的業務嚴重依賴於在中國大陸（PRC）銷售的ETUARY®，這是我們在中國大陸市場推廣的產品之一，而在競爭激烈的市場環境中，我們可能無法維持或提升ETUARY®的銷售量、價格與利潤率。
• 我們在中國大陸（PRC）市場推廣的產品ETUARY®、Etorel®與Contiva®，以及未來可能獲得批准並商業化的任何其他產品，可能無法在醫生、醫療機構、藥房、患者、第三方付款者與廣泛醫療界獲得足夠的市場接受度，而這對其商業可行性至關重要。
• 我們的業務與財務結果 largely 依賴於我們處於臨牀與前期臨牀階段的產品候選藥物的進展與成功，例如ETUARY®在中國大陸（PRC）未來適應症的應用、F573在中國大陸（PRC）的應用、Hydronidone在中國大陸（PRC）與其他市場的應用。我們面臨無法完成其臨牀開發、取得必要的監管批准或成功實現市場上市的風險，或在這些過程中可能遭遇重大挫折。
